skeleton:
Full English Breakfast Burrito

British · Easy · Makes 2 large burritos

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The full English crossed with the breakfast burrito: every component of the classic plate — sausage, bacon, black pudding, beans, egg, mushroom, tomato — wrapped in a tortilla and toasted until the package seals itself into a crisp, one-handed cylinder. The British-American hybrid that market stalls and festival breakfast vans worked out years ago, and the home version is better: the beans go in reduced-thick so they don't soak the wrap, the eggs are scrambled dry-ish instead of fried, and the whole thing finishes in a hot dry pan until the tortilla's surface crackles. This is the architecture of the full English applied to a different chassis — the components remain the components, the assembly is the new part.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The filling (one batch fills 2 wraps)

The wraps

- **Everything must be cooked and cooled slightly before wrapping.** A scalding filling steams the tortilla mid-roll and bursts it in the pan. Five minutes' rest of the components is the difference. - **Thicken the beans deliberately** — simmer them 5 minutes until they mound on a spoon. Wet beans are the number-one burrito failure; their juice wicks straight through the wrap. - **The eggs are scrambled, not fried**, and pulled just before they look done — they finish cooking in the wrap's final toasting.

Full English Breakfast Burrito

Prep: 10 minutes · Cook: 20 minutes · Total: 30 minutes · Makes 2 large burritos

Ingredients

The filling (one batch fills 2 wraps)

  • 2 pork sausages (160 g), skins removed, meat rolled into 4 mini-balls
  • 3 rashers (150 g) smoked bacon, chopped into bite pieces
  • 100 g black pudding, crumbled into large chunks
  • 4 large eggs (220 g), beaten with 2 g salt
  • 100 g baked beans, simmered 5 minutes to thicken
  • 100 g chestnut mushrooms, sliced
  • 1 tomato (120 g), deseeded and diced, juices discarded
  • 30 g mature Cheddar, grated

The wraps

  • 2 large flour tortillas (about 60 g each, 25–30 cm diameter)
  • 10 g butter, for the final toasting
  • Brown breakfast sauce, 2 tsp (10 ml) per burrito

Instructions

  1. **Cook the meats in sequence in one pan** — the fat economy in miniature. Brown the sausage balls 6–7 minutes over medium heat, then add the bacon pieces for 4 minutes, then the black pudding chunks for a final 3 minutes, each cooking in what rendered before. Lift to a plate. Checkpoint — all three meats browned and cooked, the pan carrying a slick of layered fat.
  2. **The eggs in the same pan, then the filling's assembly.** Pour the beaten eggs into the pan's fat over medium-low, scramble softly 2 minutes until barely set and still glossy, and tip onto the meat plate to stop the cooking. Wipe the pan, add a film of the butter, and quickly sauté the mushrooms 3 minutes until browned. Checkpoint — the eggs are soft-set curds (they'll finish in the wrap); the mushrooms are browned, not grey.
  3. **Build and roll.** Warm each tortilla 15 seconds in a dry pan (or 10 seconds in the microwave) until flexible. Down the centre of each, layer: half the beans in a compact line, then eggs, meats, mushrooms, diced tomato, cheese, and a stripe of brown sauce. Fold in the two sides, then roll tightly from the bottom, tucking as you go — a firm cylinder, seam-side down. Checkpoint — the wrap is a tight, even cylinder with the filling 2 cm from every edge, the seam underneath, nothing leaking. It should feel like a solid tube, not a soft parcel.
  4. **Toast to seal — 3 minutes.** Melt the remaining butter in the wiped pan over medium heat and toast each burrito seam-side down 1–2 minutes until the seam seals and the underside is crisp and blistered gold, then roll to toast every face, about 1 minute more. Rest 1 minute, then halve on the diagonal. Checkpoint — the outside is crisp and mottled gold, holding its shape at the halves, and the first cut shows the full English in cross-section — egg, sausage, bacon, black pudding, beans, the works — every layer holding its place.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Burrito burst in the panOverfilled or rolled looseCompact central stripe, tight roll, 2 cm clearance
Soggy, tearing wrapWet beans or scalding fillingReduce the beans; rest the filling 5 minutes
Falling apart when halvedNot toasted to sealThe seam-side 2-minute toast is the glue
Filling cold in the middleComponents cooked too far aheadAssembly within 5 minutes of cooking; the final toast re-heats through

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Wrap and refrigerate before the final toast** — up to 24 hours, tightly covered. Toast from cold, 4–5 minutes, turning; the cold start reheats the centre as the outside crisps. - **Variation — the vegan version:** the vegan master's shiitake bacon, tofu scramble, mushrooms, and beans in the same compact-line build; the Cheddar's slot goes to 30 g of the strongest vegan cheddar you rate. - **Variation — the hash brown core:** a thin homemade hash brown as the first layer over the beans adds the potato slot and a crisp spine through every bite. - **Serving math:** one burrito per hungry adult, halved for the plate with brown sauce for dipping, or whole, wrapped in foil, eaten walking — the breakfast van's own presentation.
